diffs.diff: header pin 4 (SEL): part says gnd, datasheet reading says io
diffs.evidence: Sensirion SPS30 datasheet v2.0 (June 2023), Table 4 'SPS30 pin assignment': pin 4 SEL 'Interface select - Leave floating to select UART / Pull to GND to select I2C'; Section 6 / Figure 6 'Typical I2C application circuit' shows SEL (4) wired to GND with the notice: 'in order to correctly select I2C as interface, the interface select (SEL) pin must be pulled to GND before or at the same time the sensor is powered up.' This model is the SPS30 in I2C mode (address 0x69, I2C driver), so SEL must be hard-wired to GND. In this library's schema role 'gnd' means 'wire this pin to GND' (src/core/autowire.ts wires role gnd pins to the board GND; checks.ts flags them if not grounded). Role 'io' would make autowire connect SEL to a GPIO input (effectively floating), which selects UART and the sensor would never answer on I2C. The second reading's 'io' describes the pin's generic select function, not the I2C wiring this part models; the pin description still documents it as interface select with a 4.0 V max (Absolute Maximum Ratings: 'Interface Select SEL -0.3 ... 4.0 V').
